hero.subtitle: When a Pinole hospital visit or treatment plan goes wrong, sorting out whether it was malpractice versus an unfortunate outcome can be confusing. We can review your situation at no cost and explain how California medical malpractice law applies to your case.

about.title: Pinole Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Pinole residents rely on a mix of local clinics and larger Contra Costa County medical centers, and most visits end without incident. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes off track, or medication is mishandled, families are often left with more questions than answers. California's MICRA law shapes these cases in specific ways — from a strict notice period before filing suit to rules about non-economic damages and requirements around expert medical testimony. Because a bad result doesn't automatically mean malpractice occurred, these claims usually hinge on whether a provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard. Our team reviews medical records, consults with qualified experts, and explains whether pursuing a claim makes sense for your situation, all without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: What to Know About Medical Malpractice Law in California

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines Apply
items.desc: California generally requires a malpractice claim within one year of discovering the injury, and never more than three years from when it happened. A 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider is also required before a lawsuit can move forward.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: Because medical decisions are technical, California law nearly always requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in on whether the standard of care was violated. We can help arrange that kind of review for you.

items.title: Damages Are Structured Under MICRA
items.desc: California's MICRA law places a cap on non-economic damages, though that cap rises each year by statute. We can walk you through how this affects your potential claim.

items.question: How do I know if what happened to me counts as malpractice?
items.answer: Not every poor outcome is the result of malpractice — sometimes complications happen even with proper care. The question is whether a provider's actions fell below the accepted medical standard, which usually requires a qualified expert's review. We can help you understand where your situation stands.

items.question: Is there a local hospital or clinic in Pinole this typically involves?
items.answer: Pinole residents often receive care at facilities throughout Contra Costa County rather than solely within city limits, so malpractice concerns can involve a range of providers. What matters most is the specific care given and whether it met accepted standards, not which building it happened in. We can look into the details of your particular treatment.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney about my case?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. We offer a free initial consultation, and our team typically works on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after an initial conversation.
